_comment: Documented exceptions to the npm audit gate. Each entry MUST have a justification + expiry. Past-expiry entries fail the build. See SUPPLY_CHAIN.md § Allowlist for the policy.
_policy: An entry exists because the fix is non-trivial (major-version bump with breaking changes, transitive in a build-only path, or no upstream fix yet). Each entry is a written commitment to revisit by the expiry date. The CI gate prints the days-to-expiry for every active entry as a forcing function.
_cleared_2026-05-25_scan: The three 2026-05-09 baseline entries (next GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8, lodash-es GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, picomatch GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p) were the fix-vs-allowlist commitments behind the recurring [cve-scan] Source HIGH findings cluster (#1374 / #1555 / #1964 / #2265). They were CLEARED — not snoozed — by the dedicated remediation PR for #2265: next 16.1.6 -> 16.2.6 (semver-minor) plus a non-force `npm audit fix` for the lodash-es / picomatch transitives. `npm audit --audit-level=high` now exits 0, so no allowlist entry is required. Per SUPPLY_CHAIN.md § 3 the fix lands with its allowlist entries removed in the same commit.
_2026-07-26_investigation: FIX WAS ATTEMPTED FIRST AND FAILED, which is why these are allowlisted rather than remediated (refs #4525). (1) next 16.2.6 -> 16.2.12 (patch, same minor) was applied to the lockfile and re-audited: it cleared NOTHING. The advisory ranges cover every published version — postcss '<=8.5.17' and next '9.3.4-canary.0 - 16.3.0-preview.7', i.e. including previews — so there is no version to upgrade to. npm's own fixAvailable proposes DOWNGRADING next to 9.3.3, which is not a fix. (2) A plain `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` made it strictly worse: 5 HIGH became 12 HIGH by pulling in an eslint major-bump cascade. Both attempts were reverted, so this commit changes no dependency versions. Re-evaluate at expiry, or sooner if a postcss > 8.5.17 lands and next vendors it.
_dev_vs_prod_note: This gate runs `npm audit` WITHOUT --omit=dev, so it blocks on dev-tooling advisories that never ship. Verified 2026-07-26 with `npm audit --omit=dev`: only 3 of these 10 advisories are in the PRODUCTION dependency graph (next, its vendored postcss, sharp). The other 7 (js-yaml, brace-expansion x2, and the eslint-chain transitives) resolve to '(empty)' under `npm ls <pkg> --omit=dev` — build/lint-time only, not present in the deployed image. Narrowing the gate to --omit=dev would be a policy change to the gate itself and is deliberately NOT bundled into this deploy-unblocking commit.
_why_this_matters: The Trivy CRITICAL gate and this npm audit gate are BOTH deploy steps in cd-source.yml. A red gate does not merely fail a scan — it silently blocks every source-kg deploy. #4522 and #4524 merged to `main` on 2026-07-26 and never reached pact.tailor.au for exactly this reason. Keep entries bounded and honest; do not extend an expiry without re-running the fix attempt.

exceptions.justification: No upstream fix exists: advisory range '<=8.5.11', and the sibling path-traversal advisory covers '<=8.5.17' — every published postcss. Reaches the prod graph ONLY as the copy vendored by next (node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss) — build-time CSS tooling. Our CSS is authored in-repo and compiled at build time; no user input reaches PostCSS stringify at runtime, and the Next standalone runtime does not run the CSS toolchain. Upgrading next to 16.2.12 does not clear it (verified 2026-07-26).
